main_issue: Who gets leave on the two working days around Hari Raya Puasa, when only two of four staff can be off and all four claim they cannot work

A-B.evidence: A (T1) and B (T2) both say they cannot change; neither speaks to the other, and B (T28) still refuses to work, as does A (T25).

A-C.evidence: A (T19) says 'This isn't about whose turn it is'; C (T21) replies 'It is about whose turn it is'. Both still want the days off.

A-D.evidence: A sympathises (T5, T11, T13) but refuses to cancel; D keeps pressing the holiday's importance (T8-T12). Later they share the point that neither can work (T24-T26).

B-C.evidence: B (T2, T28) won't work; C (T3, T15-T23) also claims the days and says it is someone else's turn. They never address each other.

B-D.evidence: B (T28) joins D's tally ('Make that four of us') after D (T26). They share the point that two must work, but both still want leave.

C-D.evidence: C (T15-T17) says it is someone else's turn; D (T16) says 'I've only been here a few months' and (T18) 'So it's their turn, then', turning it back on C. Both still claim the days.
